newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - Builder HBG '96 net seen rising.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Builder HBG '96 net seen rising.

text.p: Improved returns from civil engineering and housing will give builder HBG's profits a leg up in 1996, analysts forecast on Thursday.
The Netherlands' biggest construction group is seen posting full-year profits from ordinary operations of between 106.4 and 119.9 million guilders, with consensus at 115.7 million.
In 1995 the builder reported full-year net profit before extraordinaries of 97 million guilders.
"The biggest profit growth will have been in civil engineering, but I also expect a turnaround in housing," said Paul Verbraeken, construction analyst with ING Barings.
Although HBG does not give a profit breakdown according to sector, it is widely thought to have posted a loss on its house-building activities in 1995.

Verbraeken said housing would likely show a modest operating profit of 2.5 million guilders, compared to a year-earlier loss of five million. Along with a strong earnings rise in civil engineering, this would help propel HBG ordinary net to 116.8 million in 1996, he said.
The Dutch infrastructure market grew strongly last year, while outside Europe, HBG's Interbeton unit was also seen achieving attractive margins.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's Konrad Zomer said he also saw higher earnings from ordinary operations in 1996.
"Nearly all its subsidiaries are turning a profit -- in past years loss-making subsidiaries have consistently depressed the bottom line by some five to 10 million guilders," he said.
He said German unit Raulf Bau would likely still be loss-making, hit by the sector malaise in Germany which seemed unlikely to lift in the near term.
"For this reason I am not entirely convinced that HBG's acquisition of Wayss&Freitag is such a good move," he said. "It's a real bet on the future".
Wayss&Freitag, acquired in December 1996 and due to be consolidated from this year, posted losses of 90 million marks last year.
Zomer said it was not expected to return to profit this year or next.

Sven Smit, building analyst at Bank Labouchere, said 1996 figures would likely lean heavily on Dutch operations. "The Dutch construction market is really healthy - far healthier than elsewhere," he said.
He too expected a better result from housing, pointing to higher returns booked by sector rival Volker Stevin.
"Volker did very well in housing construction, but that is partly because they own a lot of the ground," he said.
HBG, which operates a more cautious investment policy, owned fewer sites, but nevertheless would still benefit from the housing upturn in the Netherlands, he said.
Raulf Bau's performance was also likely to have improved, he said. Smit forecast 1996 ordinary net of 118 million guilders and rated HBG a "Buy".
He said that while conditions in Germany remained difficult, Bonn was weighing up a construction sector stimulation package of 25 billion marks.
In Britain, where HBG recently acquired Higgs&Hill, the outlook was "clearly positive", he added, while the dredging sector was also on the up.
-- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000.
